clue.text: Old money not quite used up over Christmas

indicators.note: not quite means the slang word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: napoo is old army slang for finished or used up

indicators.note: over tells us the word for Christmas is turned round

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone's savings have almost all gone on the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPOO, First World War slang (from French 'il n'y en a plus') for finished, loses its last letter to NAPO; 'over' turns NOEL into LEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A napoleon was a French gold twenty-franc coin, a historical piece of currency.

clue.text: Try to make someone pay up first — someone without cover

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to dun is to press a debtor for payment
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: A creditor pursues a debtor before the debtor can hide.
explanation.walkthrough: IST is the crossword spelling of 1st.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist wears no clothes, so has nothing covering the body.

clue.text: Girl has a baby

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name
per means a or each, as in once per day

explanation.surface: A young woman gives birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby' is a verb: to cosset or spoil.
explanation.definitionFit: To baby someone is to indulge and spoil them.

clue.text: For the future, put half capital as deposit on a farm

indicators.note: half means only the first three letters of the city are kept

parts.note: London is the UK capital
a grange is a farm with its buildings

explanation.surface: Advice to invest half one's savings as a down payment on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps only the front half of the capital's name. 'For the future' describes plans that look far ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range plans are those looking far ahead in time.

clue.text: Hardy plants may be so left and ignored

definitions.text: Hardy plants may be so left

explanation.surface: A gardener leaves sturdy plants outdoors and forgets them.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy plants can be left outdoors in winter; someone left out in the cold is neglected or excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally exposed outdoors in winter, and an idiom for being excluded and neglected.

clue.text: Compensation for disconnected television

parts.note: a power supply switched off is disconnected
a TV set is a television

explanation.surface: Someone claims damages because their TV was cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set against a loss to balance it is a counterweight or recompense.

clue.text: Mushrooms, for instance, give pleasure to soldier

parts.note: fun is enjoyment or pleasure
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Treating a soldier to a good time.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms are one example of the kingdom that also includes moulds and yeasts.

clue.text: Counterfeit notes with superior press

indicators.note: with superior means the word for press sits above the notes in this down answer

parts.note: to spur is to press or urge on
IOUs are notes promising repayment

explanation.surface: Forged banknotes made with a high-quality printing press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' is positional: in a down answer it puts SPUR above IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spurious is fake, not genuine.

clue.text: We work some machines, lead rest astray

indicators.note: astray says the letters go wandering into a new order

explanation.surface: Workers complain that their leader has led the others off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges LEAD and REST. The definition has the foot pedals speaking for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot-operated levers drive old sewing machines and lathes.

clue.text: Give note in to master

indicators.note: in means the note's letters go inside the word for give

parts.note: to donate is to give
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand a message over to one's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master' is a verb here: to get the upper hand over.
explanation.definitionFit: To master is to rule over or control, the same as to hold sway.

clue.text: Cover one point? Yes!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N, north, is a point of the compass
sure is an informal way of saying yes

explanation.surface: An eager customer agreeing to buy a single item of insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: To insure something is to take out cover or a policy against loss.

clue.text: Mule demonstrated one result of spinning and weaving

definitions.text: one result of spinning and weaving

parts.note: a mule is a backless slipper
to sit in is to protest, so demonstrated gives sat in

explanation.surface: A stubborn animal put on a show of turning and twisting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mule' is not the animal but a backless slipper; SAT IN is to have staged a sit-in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Silk satin for slippers is a woven fabric made from spun thread.

clue.text: Guide the movement of ox

explanation.surface: A farmer directing a bullock along a path.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct a vehicle's course is to guide it; a castrated young bull raised for beef is a bullock-type ox.

clue.text: Empty or full, I dine irregularly

indicators.note: irregularly says these letters come out in a disordered arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eats at odd times, so their stomach is sometimes empty and sometimes full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregularly' rearranges FULL, I and DINE. 'Empty' is a verb: to void or cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify is to make void, cancelling something so it has no force, as if emptied.

clue.text: Film stars are informed

explanation.surface: A news item saying that movie celebrities have been briefed.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars of a film appear on screen in the movie; to be informed is to be kept up to date. 'are' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors appear within the movie they star in, and an idiom for being well briefed means the same.

clue.text: Zucchini, having endlessly wooed, about to win

indicators.note: about means the shortened word wraps round the other
endlessly means the last letter of the verb is dropped

parts.note: to court is to woo
to get is to win or obtain

explanation.surface: A suitor's long courtship is about to pay off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts COURTED to COURTE, which goes 'about' GET.
explanation.definitionFit: Zucchini is the American and Italian name for the same small marrow.

clue.text: Give embellishment or a title to book

parts.note: taken as written
a name is a title
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Instructions to decorate a book or give it a title.
explanation.definitionFit: To ornament is to decorate or adorn something.

clue.text: City has been read about

indicators.note: about here means the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A town has had a book read to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges BEEN READ.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a granite city in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: Bouncer in match requiring sound control

parts.note: a rubber is a match, as in bridge or tennis, decided by the best of a series

indicators.note: sound means the word for control is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to check is to control or restrain

explanation.surface: A boxing or tennis match that needs a good audio engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' is not a doorman: it is a cheque that bounces, refused by the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud payment order returned unpaid by the bank is said to bounce.

clue.text: Money we put up for a tree

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: put up in a down answer means the word is written upwards

explanation.surface: Raising funds to plant a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew nut grows on a tropical evergreen of the same name.

clue.text: Wary when drinking rum that's inferior

indicators.note: when drinking means the word for wary takes the other inside it

parts.note: shy means wary or cautious
rum is a British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Cautious about drinking poor quality spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is not the drink but the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy goods are poorly made, of low quality.

clue.text: Car pool is organised in inner city

indicators.note: organised says the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Commuters arrange to share cars into the city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges CAR, POOL and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortified citadel at the heart of an ancient Greek town, Athens most famously, was its central stronghold.

clue.text: Stop hands talking

indicators.note: talking means the word for hands is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: paws is informal for hands

explanation.surface: An instruction for workers to down tools and stop chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' is not workers but a jokey word for a person's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a brief halt or interruption.

clue.text: Grit shown by architect when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking means the architect's name is heard aloud, not spelt

parts.note: John Nash was the architect of Regency London, designer of Regent Street

explanation.surface: An architect displays determination while giving a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grit' is not pluck but a verb: to grind the teeth together. The silent G makes the sound match.
explanation.definitionFit: Gritting the teeth means grinding them together in anger or effort.

clue.text: Be sure to move about in gloomy cavern

indicators.note: move about says these letters are shifted into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A warning to keep moving around when inside a dark cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move about' rearranges BE SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Erebus is the dark region of the underworld through which the dead pass.

clue.text: Sewed in the way desired

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
itched means longed or desired, as in itching to go

explanation.surface: Someone did their needlework exactly as they wished.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining fabric with needle and thread is the act of stitching.

clue.text: Money once required by craftsman

explanation.surface: An artisan demanding payment for their work in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: A TANNER was British slang for the old sixpence coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an old sixpenny piece; also a worker who turns hides into leather.

clue.text: Going down the road

parts.note: under means below, the same as down
a way is a road or path

explanation.surface: A direction to travel along a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A project in progress is said to be moving or in motion.
